source: Newly attached image (black silhouette GABRIEL render with glowing red eyes on a white background)
processing: Non-generative alpha reconstruction only -- no AI redraw/regeneration, no new content synthesized. The uploaded file already carried an alpha channel, but it was a hard binary 0/255 mask that had clearly been produced by a naive white-threshold on a flattened white-background render: fully-transparent pixels were correctly 0, but many edge/anti-aliased pixels that were originally a partial blend toward white got forced to alpha=255 while KEEPING their blended (light gray to near-white) RGB color, which reads as a visible white/gray fringe or halo around the whole silhouette once composited over anything other than white (checked: 0.36% of nominally-opaque pixels had brightness > 200, concentrated along the long, spiky wing/claw edges).
cleanup_method: Per-pixel classification, no manual retouching: (1) redness = R - max(G,B); pixels with redness > 15 (the glowing red eyes) are kept fully opaque (alpha=255) with their original RGB untouched, preserving the eye glow exactly as supplied. (2) All other originally-opaque (non-red) pixels are treated as a black-foreground/white-background blend: recovered alpha = clamp(255 - brightness, 0, 255) where brightness = mean(R,G,B), and RGB is forced to pure black (0,0,0). This is a direct, deterministic mathematical inversion (alpha_orig ~= 1 - brightness/255 for a black-on-white blend), not a synthesized value -- a pixel that was nearly pure black stays alpha~255 opaque black; a pixel that was mostly white (the fringe) correctly resolves to near-0 alpha (transparent) instead of a light gray rim; a genuine antialiased edge pixel gets a smoothly graded partial alpha fading to black, which reads as a clean edge against ANY background (dark or light) instead of a white-halo cutout. (3) Originally fully-transparent pixels (alpha_orig==0) are zeroed (alpha=0, rgb=(0,0,0)) regardless of whatever stray RGB they carried.
verification: Composited the result over solid dark navy, solid magenta, and solid mid-gray test backgrounds and visually confirmed: no white/gray fringe or halo anywhere along the silhouette (including the many small wing-feather/claw tips), the body reads as a clean near-black silhouette, and the red eye glow is fully preserved and vivid.

body_landmarks.measurement_method: Alpha-channel scan of the cleaned image restricted to the head/torso x-band (540-660, matching the red-eye bbox 557-646 with margin) for head_top_y and center_x; feet_bottom_y is the single lowest opaque row overall.

usage: assets/boss/dark_phase.png is used EXCLUSIVELY for GABRIEL's DARK PHASE state -- never for normal IDLE/WALK/ATTACK/DEFENSE, and never mixed into the existing front/back DOWN-CINEMATIC system (assets/boss/cinematic_pose.png / cinematic_pose_back.png), which remain completely separate and unmodified. Drawn at its own aspect ratio (1152/1728), scaled via DARKPHASE_SCALE (derived from this image's own body-landmark fill fraction relative to the front CINEMATIC image's, same method as CINEMATIC_BACK_SCALE) so it reads at roughly the same on-screen body size as the normal boss sprite -- see DARKPHASE_SCALE in game.js.
